title: Deser and Arnowitt graviton essay

tellings.quote: The pair wrote a paper about these theoretical gravitons in their 1954 winning essay for the Gravity Research Foundation.

plain: In 1954 the physicists Stanley Deser and Richard Arnoux won an essay prize from the Gravity Research Foundation, a group that gave awards for work on gravity, with a paper about gravitons, the theoretical particles thought to carry gravity. Michels tells this himself, citing The G-Engines Are Coming, a 1956 piece, along with a man named Michael Gladish. He brings it up because, if serious physicists were working on gravity this way in the 1950s, it would fit his case that people were looking hard into controlling gravity back then.
